## \## Overview

Script 3 generates all ATAC-seq-specific visualisations from the annotated peak files produced by Script 1. No re-annotation is performed --- all genomic feature and distance information is read directly from the Script 1 output files, ensuring complete consistency between annotation and visualisation. Significant peaks are defined throughout as padj ≤ 0.05 with no fold change filter.

The script produces five categories of output: genomic feature pie charts, combined annotation bar charts, distance-to-TSS bidirectional bar charts, Manhattan plots, and circos plots.

## Methods summary

### Annotation category simplification

ChIPseeker annotation labels contain detailed transcript and exon information (e.g. "Intron (ENSGALT\.../ENSGALG\..., intron 3 of 12)"). These are simplified to seven clean categories using pattern matching: Promoter, Exon, Intron, Downstream, Distal Intergenic, 5' UTR, and 3' UTR. The same simplification is applied identically across all six comparisons.

### Genomic feature pie charts

One pie chart per comparison. Peaks filtered to padj ≤ 0.05. The legend includes all seven feature categories in every chart regardless of whether a category is present in a given comparison, ensuring a consistent legend across all six charts.

### Annotation bar charts

Three 100% stacked bar charts showing the proportion of significant peaks in each genomic feature category. Each bar represents one comparison. Three versions: all six comparisons combined, Group 1 only (antagomirs vs scramble), and Group 2 only (antagomirs vs each other).

### Distance to TSS bar charts

One bidirectional bar chart per comparison. The distanceToTSS column from Script 1 is converted from base pairs to kilobases and binned into 12 distance bands: \\\< −100, −100 to −10, −10 to −5, −5 to −3, −3 to −1, −1 to 0, 0 to 1, 1 to 3, 3 to 5, 5 to 10, 10 to 100, and \\\> 100 kb. Upstream bands are coloured Blue and downstream bands Vermillion. The Y axis is fixed at 40% across all comparisons for direct visual comparability.

### Manhattan plots

One Manhattan plot per comparison plus a combined 2×3 panel. All peaks are shown regardless of significance. Non-significant peaks are displayed as small grey points. Significant peaks (padj ≤ 0.05) are coloured by chromatin change direction: Vermillion for opening (positive log2FoldChange) and Blue for closing (negative log2FoldChange). The Y axis shows −log10(padj) with no cap --- the maximum value across all comparisons is 13.6. The combined panel uses a fixed Y axis limit of 15 so all six comparisons are directly comparable. A dashed threshold line is drawn at −log10(0.05). One Excel file is saved per comparison containing all peaks with a significant (TRUE/FALSE) column to allow identification of individual data points.

### Circos plots

Three circular peak density plots showing the genome-wide distribution of significant ATAC-seq peaks. Peak density is calculated per 1 Mb window per chromosome and normalised 0-1 within each chromosome so all chromosomes are visually comparable regardless of size. Three versions: all six comparisons, Group 1 only, and Group 2 only.
